column11: Deuteronomy 32:9: ‘For the ETERNAL’s portion is this people;Jacob, God’s own allotment.’ Context and connection to Likkutei Maamarim: In Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 6, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Deuteronomy 32:9) to illuminate his argument here (“and "Jacob is the lot of His inheritance" Deuteronomy 32:9, "for Hashem's portion is His people" ibid.. And this corresponds to the tefillin of Israel wherein is inscribed "Hear, O Israel... Hashem is One"...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source grounds the spiritual dynamic of Torah, Israel's sanctity, and divine service developed in this discourse of Likkutei Maamarim.
column13: And this is: "For Hashem's portion is His people; Jacob is the lot of His inheritance" (Devarim 32:9); and as stated in Shir HaShirim Rabbah (5:2) on "I sleep, but my heart wakes" (Shir HaShirim 5:2): "The Holy One is the heart of Israel, as it is said: God is the rock of my heart, and my portion forever" (Tehillim 73:26).

column15: “Of the Rock that begot you, you were unmindful (teshi), and you forgot God Who brought you forth” (Deuteronomy 32:18). The Blessed Name created the faculty of forgetfulness for man’s benefit—as taught in Kohelet Rabbah and Pesachim 54b—so that a person may continually renew his Torah learning as if for the first time and release past grief; the sin is only when one misuses forgetfulness to neglect his Creator.
